correctness.rationale: For every real 0<s<1 and positive bidirectional b_i,c_i with four distinct ratios, the exact trace decomposition sI+tX_i gives the single schedule-dependent term t^4 prod(c_i)(r_{pi1}r_{pi3}+r_{pi2}r_{pi4}); determinant is permutation-invariant. The two algebraic pair-gap factorizations are strictly positive and Perron monotonicity at fixed determinant converts them to three strict multiplier classes of eight. Products increase entrywise with contact scale t>0, each Perron root runs continuously and strictly from s^4<1 to infinity, giving three unique strictly separated crossing times and the stated reversal intervals. One through three seasons have order-independent trace and determinant. Both off-diagonal coefficients vary in the exact rational counterexample; 7,227 exact checks corroborate identities and the crossing signs, not infinity.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalence was checked under cyclic rotation, reversal, simultaneous reindexing, and diagonal similarity. The classified full bidirectional ratio family and all-parameter threshold separation are not implied by the constant-direction formula as stated.

originality.rationale: The accessible 2012 primary full text provides a periodic stability criterion in a higher-dimensional mosquito-only model, and 2009 and 2014 primary metadata concern general growth or different Ross–Macdonald equations, without verified statement of this exact two-way ratio ordering and universal intensity threshold separation. Closest prior narrow comparisons fix one seasonal infection direction, or use a distinct constant-dispersal growth family; they are not claimed as new. The general two-direction extension is not an implication of those statements as presented. This is a self-review best-knowledge originality judgment with explicit incomplete full-text and broader-theorem risks, not historical priority certification.

value.rationale: The four-season ordering classification determines for every admissible independently varying host-to-vector and vector-to-host seasonal transmission profile which calendars have greater local invasion multipliers. The theorem further proves three noncoincident critical contact-intensity values for every configuration, so there are nonempty intensity intervals where timing alone reverses the invasion verdict; four is a sharp minimal horizon. This is a motivated structural law across a full positive-parameter family rather than a single instance or routine numerical gain. Limits: idealized local discrete-time model and no field-control conclusion.
